h1: Iron Fence Dallas: Wrought Iron and Ornamental Steel Fences
heroSub: Real wrought iron, welded ornamental steel or aluminum: what Dallas-area firms advertise for each, what the City says about front yards, and how to compare written quotes. Call now on (214) 555-0137.
introHtml:
Pricing an iron fence in Dallas usually comes down to one question: what metal is the quote actually for? 'Wrought iron' is used for real forged iron, for welded ornamental steel and, loosely, for aluminum that is made to look like iron. The price, the rust risk and the repair options are different for each.

White Rock Fence Co is advertising that points Dallas homeowners to independent fence contractors. It builds nothing itself, and the contractor who quotes your job sets the price. This page covers the materials, how a job is scoped, what the City of Dallas says about front yards and pool barriers, and what to expect for gates, painting and rust repair. For cost context across fence types, see the Dallas fence cost guide.

features.title: The metal is named on the quote
features.desc: Real wrought iron, tubular steel and aluminum all get called 'iron'. A quote you can compare names the bar, the picket size and the coating.

features.title: Posts set for expansive clay
features.desc: Much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture. Ask each contractor to write down the footing they plan and how panels follow a slope.

features.title: Finish and rust protection spelled out
features.desc: Rust starts at welds, cut ends and chipped coating. A good quote says what primer and topcoat go on and how the cut ends are treated.

features.title: Gates as separate line items
features.desc: Walk gates, double drive gates and automatic gates are priced differently. Hinges, latch and any opener wiring should each be written down.

features.title: City and HOA checks up front
features.desc: Dallas limits front-yard fences to 4 ft, and many HOAs control fence type. Ask who files the permit and who gets the HOA approval before you sign.

features.title: Repair and repaint scope
features.desc: Rust repair, a bent panel or a sagging gate can be quoted by the section or by the foot. Photos and a rough length make the first conversation faster.

sections.heading: Wrought iron, ornamental steel or aluminum: what you are buying
sections.html:
Real wrought iron is forged and sits at the top of the price range. Most iron-look fences around Dallas are welded ornamental steel or aluminum, and firms use the labels differently. King of Kings Fence, a Dallas-area firm, lists 'true wrought iron' at $60 to $100+ per linear foot in its 2026 guide, against $25 to $45 for steel, $30 to $50 for galvanized steel and $20 to $40 for iron-look aluminum.

Steel is strong and can be welded back together, but it rusts wherever the coating breaks, so the finish decides how it ages. Aluminum does not rust, which helps near sprinklers and pool splash, but it is lighter, so ask how the gate frame and hinges are built. Either way, ask the contractor to name the metal and the coating in writing.

Here is what individual firms advertise for installed metal fence, per linear foot. These are their figures, not quotes from this site, and they do not agree with each other.

  • TX Fence & Deck (Wylie, serves DFW, 21 May 2026): standard residential tubular steel $30 to $45; commercial-grade $40 to $60; custom scrollwork $55 to $85.
  • King of Kings Fence (2026 guide): $25 to $60 for a 4 ft fence from basic to premium custom, and $30 to $70 for 6 ft.
  • Ergeon, Dallas County page: metal or aluminum fence $43 to $52.
  • Ergeon, across all its markets (not Dallas): steel $55 to $95, aluminum $36 to $65.

Get two or three written quotes with the same height, the same run and the same gate count so the totals can be compared. More on how prices are quoted is in the fence cost guide.

sections.heading: How an iron fence job is scoped, step by step
sections.html:
Whether you are writing a purchase order or just comparing quotes, the same items need to be in writing. Ask for them by run (front, side, rear), because the height and the rules differ from one run to the next.

  • Layout: linear feet per run, height, and a sketch showing the property line, easements, sidewalks, driveways and any corner-lot visibility triangle.
  • Utility locates: Texas811 says Texas law requires you or your contractor to call 811 two business days before digging, and that a hired contractor is responsible for the call.
  • Posts and footings: the contractor's written footing plan, and how panels follow grade on a slope.
  • Panels: bar and picket size, picket spacing, post spacing, and whether the panels are welded or bolted in place.
  • Finish: primer, topcoat, color, and how cut ends and welds are treated.
  • Gates: number, width, hinge and latch hardware, and any opener.
  • Paperwork and cleanup: who files the permit, who gets HOA approval, and what happens to the old fence.

The City of Dallas permit guide says applications for fences require a general contractor to be listed as the contractor. Richardson and Irving say contractors must be registered with the city. Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, so ask for city registration where it applies and for proof of insurance.

sections.heading: Front yards, height limits and pool fences: what the City says
sections.html:
Open iron panels are a natural fit for front-yard rules, because the Dallas code cares about how open a panel is. Under Dallas Development Code Sec. 51A-4.602, a fence in a required front yard in residential districts other than multifamily may not exceed four feet, and a panel less than 50 percent open may not sit within five feet of the front lot line. Corner lots and driveways have a separate visibility-triangle rule covering anything between 2-1/2 ft and 8 ft in height.

The City's fence permit checklist says a permit is required above 4 ft in a front yard or 6 ft in all other locations, with a 9 ft maximum. Historic, conservation and planned development districts have extra requirements. Confirm your lot with the City at (214) 948-4480 and with your HOA before you sign anything.

On HOAs, Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 stops an association from banning a perimeter fence, but it can still regulate the type of fencing. Get written approval of the style and color first.

Nearby cities set their own limits, each from the city's own page. Garland allows wood or wrought iron up to 3.5 ft with open spacing in a front yard, Richardson 3 ft decorative, Plano 40 inches at least 50 percent open, Irving 48 inches with 50 percent see-through, Mesquite 3.5 ft and Carrollton 36 inches. See the local pages for Plano, Garland, Richardson and Irving.

Pool fences are a separate permit in Dallas. The City checklist asks for barrier height, material, clearances and the height and location of the gate latch release, but it does not list dimensions, so do not take a number from a blog. For comparison only, Richardson's page says its pool fences need to be at least 4 ft with no opening over 4 inches and self-closing, self-latching gates. That is Richardson's rule, not Dallas's.

sections.heading: Gates, openers, painting and rust repair
sections.html:
Iron fences tend to fail in a few predictable places: rust at welds and along the bottom rail, chipped coating, bent pickets after a mower or a vehicle, and gates that sag on their hinges or no longer meet the latch. Walk the line each spring and after hard storms, and touch up bare metal as soon as you see it. North Texas storms with 58 mph winds count as severe, according to the National Weather Service.

Gates are where most of the money goes. TX Fence & Deck advertises a single swing walk gate at $400 to $800 and a double-drive driveway gate at $900 to $2,500+, with an opener add-on of $800 to $2,000. King of Kings Fence says operators can add another $1,000 to $3,000. Ft Worth Fence & Patio, a Fort Worth firm, advertises $300 to $2,000 for metal fence repairs.

Catch gate trouble early. TX Fence & Deck says issues caught early cost $100 to $300 to fix, against $1,000+ for motor replacements. Power wiring for a gate opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence. For a gate that has stopped working, see gate repair in Dallas.

No Dallas firm price for repainting iron was sourced, so ask for it as its own line: remove loose rust, spot-prime bare steel, then topcoat. Wood-staining prices do not apply to metal. Call now on (214) 555-0137 with a rough length, the height and a photo of the fence or gate, and an independent Dallas fence contractor can quote it in writing. Installing a new fence line? See fence installation in Dallas.

faq.q: How much does an iron fence cost in Dallas?
faq.a: It depends on the metal, height and style, and firms disagree. TX Fence & Deck advertises $30 to $45 per linear foot installed for standard residential tubular steel and $55 to $85 for custom scrollwork. King of Kings Fence advertises $25 to $60 per linear foot, and Ergeon's Dallas County page shows $43 to $52 for metal or aluminum. Get two or three written quotes, because none of these is a quote for your fence.

faq.q: How tall can an iron fence be in a Dallas front yard?
faq.a: Under Dallas Development Code Sec. 51A-4.602, a fence in a required front yard in residential districts other than multifamily may not exceed four feet. A panel less than 50 percent open may not sit within five feet of the front lot line. Corner lots have a visibility-triangle rule too, so confirm your lot with the City at (214) 948-4480 and with your HOA.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for an iron fence in Dallas?
faq.a: The City of Dallas checklist says a permit is required for a fence above 4 ft in a front yard or above 6 ft elsewhere, and the maximum is 9 ft. Its guide says no permit is needed within those limits except in areas such as historic, conservation and planned development districts. Other cities differ: Richardson requires one at 2.5 ft or taller, Mesquite above 2 ft, and Irving for any new or replacement fence.

faq.q: Is wrought iron better than steel or aluminum?
faq.a: It costs far more. King of Kings Fence lists true wrought iron at $60 to $100+ per linear foot, against $25 to $45 for steel and $20 to $40 for iron-look aluminum. Firms use 'wrought iron' for different things, so ask what the bar is made of and what coating goes on it before you compare totals.

faq.q: What does an automatic iron gate cost?
faq.a: King of Kings Fence says an operator can add $1,000 to $3,000 to the gate, and TX Fence & Deck advertises an opener add-on of $800 to $2,000 on top of a $900 to $2,500+ double-drive gate. Running power to a remote gate can add to that, and power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence. These are firms' advertised figures, not quotes from this site.
